# Specialty types

> A specialty is the type an agent was created as (`Agent.specialty`). The platform ships one built-in type, `specialist`; any other type is registered by an `AdminExtension`. There is no manifest format: coding defaults (crons, plugins, tools) are supplied as code by the extension that registers the type.

## What a type is

The built-in type is a small typed record, `SPECIALIST_TYPE` in `lib/specialist-type.ts`:

| Field | Value for `specialist` | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `specialist` | the value stored in `Agent.specialty` |
| `displayName` | `Specialist Agent` | the new-agent picker |
| `templatesDir` | `agent-types/specialist/templates/` | the runtime's workspace template lookup (`resolveTemplatesDir()` in `runtime/setup.ts`) |
| `tools` | `Bash`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `Agent` | seeded as `AgentTool` rows when an agent is created |
| `requiredEnv` | `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | `missingRequiredEnv` on the agent detail (key names only, informational, never blocks create) |

`specialist` has no system crons and no type-specific plugins (every new agent still gets the platform default `agent-platform@app-vitals-agent`; see [agent-types.md](agent-types.md#default-plugins)). It is specialized after creation through the admin API.

## Type validity

`admin/src/specialty-types.ts` resolves a stored specialty to its record:

- **`tryGetType(specialty)`** returns the record for `specialist` and for the configured default type (`SHIPWRIGHT_DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPE`), and `undefined` for anything else. `POST /admin/agents` and `POST /agents` use it, together with `hasExtensionType()`, to reject an unknown requested type with `invalid_type` before any row is created.
- **`getType(specialty)`** never throws and resolves every stored value, including legacy ones such as `coding`, to the specialist floor. Required-env reporting uses it, so no stored specialty can break an agent read.
- **`listTypes()`** feeds the new-agent picker; `withExtensionAgentTypes()` merges the types an extension declares through `agentTypes()`.

## Images per specialty

Agent images are resolved per specialty, not shared: with provisioning enabled, `resolveImage()` (`admin/src/agent-image-map.ts`) picks each agent's image from the `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGES` map (its own specialty entry, then a `default` entry, then the single `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_IMAGE`/`_IMAGE_TAG` fallback). Provisioning, drift detection and reconcile all use it, so an agent's pod image follows its stored `Agent.specialty`.

## Changing an agent's specialty

`PATCH /agents/:id` accepts `{"specialty": "<type>"}`. It is platform-admin only (403 for session members), returns 422 when the type is not known to the specialty registry, and is a no-op (no reconcile, no log) when the value equals the current specialty. On a real change it:

1. writes `Agent.specialty`;
2. runs `reconcileSystemCrons(agentId)` against the new type: system crons the new type does not declare are deleted (with their `AgentCronRun` history), and crons the type does declare are created or updated in place. Crons with `system=false` (user crons) are never touched, so a cron that already exists as a user cron survives the move;
3. reconciles the in-cluster workload with the new specialty (self-hosted agents have none), so the pod is recreated on the image `resolveImage()` maps to the new specialty.

A failure in step 2 or 3 does not fail the request: the row is already written, and the message is returned in the response `warning` field; the next full reconcile converges it. One audit line is logged per change (agent id, old and new specialty, caller name; never the key).

## Extension-registered types

An `AdminExtension` (`admin/src/admin-extension.ts`) adds a type with two optional hooks:

- `agentTypes()` lists `{name, displayName}` entries the picker offers and create accepts.
- `specialtyDefaults(name)` supplies `{crons, tools, plugins}`. Create-time seeding uses the returned tools/plugins instead of the type's tools floor, and the cron reconcile uses the returned crons. A field left undefined falls back to the built-in type for that field (no crons, no plugins).

Extension types use the specialist floor for required env. Their workspace templates are looked up at `<specialties dir>/<name>/templates/` (see [agent-types.md](agent-types.md#templates)).

## Rules

### FLOOR_TOOLS are outside type authority

The agent runtime always grants a fixed set of 7 **floor tools** (`Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Skill`, `TodoWrite`; the `FLOOR_TOOLS` constant in `runtime/claude.ts`) regardless of a type's `tools`. A type's `tools` are additive on top of the floor and request the high-privilege tools that are not floor-granted (`Bash`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `Agent`, `Monitor`). See [agent-ops.md](agent-ops.md) for the full floor-tools versus allowed-tools model.

### Types never contain secret values

`requiredEnv` is a list of key names only. Secret values are supplied per agent through the admin service's encrypted `AgentEnv` store.

### Crons

Crons come only from an extension's `specialtyDefaults()`. Under the platform's own rule for published defaults, a new cron ships `enabled: false` so it cannot fire unexpectedly on existing agents; enable it per agent once verified.
